newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN REAL SOFTWARE TO HAVE BUMPER START.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN REAL SOFTWARE TO HAVE BUMPER START.

text.p: Shares in Belgian information technology (IT) services firm Real Software were indicated sharply higher on Tuesday, their first day of trading on the Brussels bourse's second-tier double-fixing cash market.
The stock was quoted at a bid/ask of 2,500 Belgian francs at 0940 GMT, down slightly from earlier indications of 2,600, but well above the 1,500 franc issue price.
Its offer of 420,000 shares was oversubscribed 12 times, the company said in May.

At the issue price the company was valued at 1.85 billion francs. The software development and implementation firm has 400 staff, annual turnover of some 1.2 billion francs, of which one third is realised abroad, and net profit of 102 million francs.
Analysts have rated the share a 'buy' in view of Real Software's prospects. The company itself foresees annual growth in sales and profit of 10 to 20 percent.

KB Securities analyst Johan Pede said recently he expected turnover to grow by 16.5 percent in 1997, 20.9 percent in 1998 and 18.8 percent in 1999. The EPS growth rate was seen at 20.8 percent in 1997, 23.0 percent in 1998 and 20.6 percent in 1999.
Brokers Cels Guigon Securities said that at a price/earnings ratio of 15 for 1997 and 12.2 for 1998 the share was very cheap compared to European competitors which have an average 1997 p/e of 20.8.
"Based on the discounted cash flow method the theoretical value is 1,705 francs per share. We expect the share to rise by at least 20 percent in the near term," Cels said.

A spokeswoman for the Brussels bourse later told Reuters the share had been given an indicative first fixing price of 2,600 francs, indicative because demand has been so high that bourse limits on price movements had been triggered.
She said the bourse had set a one-off limit for the share of 30 percent, but even that had been exceeded and the stock exchange had had to resort to an indicative fixing at 0915 GMT.
For the second fixing at 1315 GMT a limit of five percent would apply, in line with regular practice.
